context.objective: Enable employees to submit expenses in the existing employee portal, route them to managers for approval, and enable Finance to handle reimbursement.
context.current_task: Establish the project scope and requirements for ExpPay.
in_scope: Employee expense submission in the existing employee portal
Expense categorization using QuickBooks expense types
Out-of-pocket expense reimbursement through scheduled payroll deposits
Revision and resubmission of rejected expenses
systems: Existing company QuickBooks configuration (authoritative expense type source)
authoritative_sources: User-provided approval policy and GAL mode selection dated 2026-09-21
User-provided threshold, category, and receipt rules dated 2026-09-21
User-provided payment, resubmission, and submission-timing rules dated 2026-09-21
User-provided timing, QuickBooks source, and payroll mechanism status dated 2026-09-21
User-provided required-field and deferred workflow decisions dated 2026-09-21
confirmed_business_rules: Employees submit expenses in the existing employee portal.
Corporate card expenses of $25 or less are automatically approved.
Corporate card expenses over $25 and under $101 require approval by the employee's direct manager.
Corporate card expenses of $101 or more require approval by the direct manager and the next-level manager.
Expenses not on a corporate card always require approval by the employee's direct manager.
Expenses not on a corporate card that are $101 or more also require approval by the next-level manager.
Expense categories must mirror QuickBooks expense types because Finance needs those categories for tax reporting.
No additional category-specific limits have been defined.
Employees must attach a receipt for expenses of $26 or more.
Corporate card expenses are paid directly to the card vendor.
For employee-paid out-of-pocket expenses, reimbursement is included in the employee's next scheduled payroll deposit after the expense is approved.
Rejected expenses can be revised and resubmitted.
Expenses must be submitted within 60 days of the expense date.
Expense types come from the company's existing QuickBooks configuration.
Employees must provide the expense date, amount, payment type, and expense category for each expense.

open_questions.question: What process or system transfers an approved out-of-pocket expense into the employee payroll deposit, and what role does ExpPay play in that transfer?
Who may reject an expense, and must the rejection include a reason for the employee?
Which expense status changes require notifications, and who receives them?
Must an employee provide a description for an expense?

decision_debt.decision: Finance and Payroll must determine the technical mechanism for transferring approved out-of-pocket expenses into payroll.
Determine whether expense descriptions are required.
Determine who may reject an expense and whether a rejection reason is required.
Determine which workflow notifications are required and who receives them.

resolved_history.question: Which GAL requirements depth should ExpPay use?
What approval policy should apply to submitted expenses?
resolved_history.resolution: Approval varies by corporate-card status and expense amount, as recorded in confirmed business rules; fractional threshold gaps remain tracked in Q-004.

resolved_history.question: How should amounts between $25.00 and $26.00 and between $100.00 and $101.00 be approved when an expense includes cents?
resolved_history.resolution: Use continuous approval thresholds: corporate-card expenses up to and including $25 are automatically approved; expenses over $25 and under $101 require the direct manager; expenses of $101 or more require the direct manager and next-level manager. Non-corporate-card expenses always require the direct manager and also require the next-level manager at $101 or more.

resolved_history.question: What is the authoritative list or source for the QuickBooks expense types that ExpPay must mirror?
resolved_history.resolution: Use the company's existing QuickBooks configuration as the authoritative source for expense types.

resolved_history.question: What event starts the 60-day expense submission period?
resolved_history.resolution: The 60-day submission period starts on the expense date.

resolved_history.question: What information must an employee provide for each submitted expense?
resolved_history.resolution: Employees must provide expense date, amount, payment type, and expense category. A receipt must be attached when required by the receipt rule. Whether a description is required remains deferred in Q-010.

decisions.decision: Use STANDARD GAL mode for ExpPay.
Use continuous monetary thresholds for expense approval routing.
Use the company's existing QuickBooks configuration as the authoritative expense type source.
Measure the 60-day submission period from the expense date.
Require expense date, amount, payment type, and expense category for every expense, plus a receipt when the receipt rule applies.
